items.title: William "Ba Ba" Ridgley Interview, 1961-04-07
items.q: And we played Trankina's Restorant after Pierron left out there.

ctx.x: Didn't have a back to it or anything?

No. Well yeah, something like that to keep them falling out. We had a back. That's very good. Things like that. Then when we played in the hour playing on Friday, June of 18, 19 and 24, Gitt's aerial circus used to come here every summer. And Mr. George Gates, the president of that company, told us that we were the first one that played live music in the air, Tuxi the band. Of course there had been piano players and different things like that, records and so on, like you said, but we were the first one to play…
Did you know a fellow named Henry Lambert way back?

items.title: William "Ba Ba" Ridgley Interview, 1959-06-02
items.q: Peter Ron was a member of our band at that time.

ctx.x: For the booking agent. For the group. For the group, really.

Now we are... Peter Ron never was a member of our band. Peter Booker was a member of our band. He played violin. Yeah. But at this time they make this picture. Peter Ron was a member of our band at that time. He never was. Now you're showing the name of your son of the cornet players? Oh yes. What do you mean? Louis Armstrong. Mark Carey. When did you work with Armstrong? Just... never was a member. But he jobbed around with us in Southern Standard Place at times. He was young. He was very young. He hadn't…
St. Sarah in the band, on the band, John?
